newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: France warns on Bangui killings, backs mediation.
newsitem.headline: France warns on Bangui killings, backs mediation.

text.p: France says it remains committed to efforts to broker peace in the Central African Republic despite the killing by army mutineers in the capital of two unarmed French soldiers on a multinational mediation team.

But a terse statement issued in Paris after the Saturday morning shooting warned France would not tolerate such attacks against its soldiers, adding that they were working to bring peace and democracy to the impoverished nation.

Mediators, who met representatives of embattled President Ange-Felix Patasse on Saturday, said they would press on with their efforts to defuse the former French colony's third army revolt within a year.

"We are continuing our efforts... we are continuing our meetings," Colonel Alioune Ibaba, Gabonese coordinator of a follow-up committee set up by four mediating African heads of state, told Reuters after meeting Patasse supporters.

Witnesses said French troops, who intervened in an earlier army revolt in May to keep Patasse in power, had reinforced at flashpoints in the city, deploying tanks and armoured personnel carriers. French helicopters hovered overhead.
A French Defence Ministry statement denounced the killings as a "cowardly murder".

Sources close to efforts to end the latest army revolt, which began on November 16, said the two soldiers had been part of a multinational inspection team visiting a barricade where a 22-year-old civilian protester was killed earlier in the day.

Witnesses reported that a mutineer opening fire on the soldiers, whose visit to the barricade came during a tense morning lull that followed clashes between French troops, mutineers and civilian protesters who support them.
The team included officers from Chad and Burkina Faso.

"France reiterates its support for the action of this committee of African heads of state and will not tolerate such attacks against its soldiers, who are working for peace and democracy," the French Defence Ministry said in a statement.
French sources, quoted by Radio France International, said French troops intervened earlier on Saturday after youths had attacked homes and business of foreigners.

The mutinies began over pay but have turned into a campaign to oust Patasse, a civilian elected in 1993 after the advent of multi-party politics. Patasse has refused to resign. Hundreds of people have died in violence associated with the revolts.
